title: Шеф на диете  (The Chef on a Diet)

segments.t: Back in the kitchen, Fedya invites Chef Barinov to share their staff meal of pasta and sausage, but Viktor announces he is on a diet. When Barinov demands an honest answer from Max about his weight, Max's blunt truth leaves the chef fuming.
Шеф, а вы как раз вовремя.
У нас тут французское блюдо. Хотите?
Нет, спасибо. Я сегодня на диете.
Шеф, вам это зачем?
Хочу немножко привести себя в порядок.
Шеф, вы и так выглядите супер!
Скажи, только честно.
Я толстый?
Да, шеф, вы толстый.
Слышь, ты когда врал, мне больше нравился!
Вы сами спросили, шеф.
Иди работай, дятел!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Шеф, а вы как раз вовремя.

'Chef, you are right on time.' Fedya explains that Barinov is right on time, keeping his voice calm and direct. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
У нас тут французское блюдо. Хотите?
'We have a French dish here. Do you want some?' When Fedya asks if they have a French dish here, Barinov has to answer fast.
Нет, спасибо. Я сегодня на диете.
'No, thank you. I am on a diet today.' Barinov explains that he is on a diet today, keeping his voice calm and direct.
Шеф, вам это зачем?
'Chef, why do you need that?' Asking why Barinov needs is how Fedya puts Barinov on the spot. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Хочу немножко привести себя в порядок.
'I want to get myself in shape a bit.' Wanting to get himself in shape a bit is how Barinov lays out the situation for Fedya.
Шеф, вы и так выглядите супер!
'Chef, you already look super!' Over the kitchen and the answer, Fedya lets his real feelings show. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Скажи, только честно.
'Tell me, only honestly.' Saying that Fedya should tell him only honestly is how Barinov sets the tone with Fedya.
Я толстый?
'Am I fat?' Over the answer and the kitchen, Barinov presses Fedya for a straight answer.
Да, шеф, вы толстый.
'Yes, chef, you are fat.' Saying that Barinov is fat is how Max sets the tone with Barinov. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Слышь, ты когда врал, мне больше нравился!

'Listen, I liked you better when you lied!' Because he liked Fedya better when Fedya lied, Barinov does not bother softening the blow for Fedya. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Вы сами спросили, шеф.
'You asked me yourself, chef.' Mentioning that Barinov asked him themselves moves the talk in a new direction.
Иди работай, дятел!

'Go work, blockhead!' Insisting that Fedya should go work blockhead shows Barinov is not backing down. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

Скажи, только честно.
Я толстый?
Да, шеф, вы толстый.
Слышь, ты когда врал, мне больше нравился!

Иди работай, дятел!
That brings this funny kitchen moment to a close. See you next time!
Пока!
